---
name: apple-hig
description: Use when designing, implementing, or reviewing interfaces for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, CarPlay, or other Apple system experiences using Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Routes to current platform, foundation, pattern, component, input, and technology guidance.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: AyushRajSinghParihar
  source: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines
---

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support, product feasibility, or platform adaptation, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. Before finalizing the route, search the [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md)
   for the task's concepts as well as component or framework names. Its trigger
   descriptions connect everyday product requests to Apple's topic names; users
   need not name an Apple framework. Read the owning family and matching topic
   procedure before its supporting reference. Search relevant rows instead of
   loading the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

Platform: macOS. Three arbitrary columns show search results, status and file size, yet users expect a parent-to-child hierarchy. Choosing a child loses its parent context. Very long folder names and empty folders are common.

# Apple HIG: Translate information hierarchy into containers

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Map records, groups, selection and supporting detail before choosing lists, collections, split views, tabs or disclosure. Open the procedure for the candidate container.
2. Separate grouping from navigation: a box organizes related content; a split view coordinates hierarchical panes; disclosure reveals optional detail. Do not use a container merely because space is available.
3. For resizing, large content and empty states, retain a coherent selection and route back. Identify minimum useful pane/content behavior from the task rather than fixed screenshots.
4. Deliver the hierarchy, selection model, adaptive layout decisions and a patch or verification matrix covering narrow and expanded states.

## Enter the topic procedure

Read the selected topic’s SKILL.md before its supporting guidance. For a review,
inspect actual evidence and return findings; for an implementation request, make
the authorized change; for design or adaptation, produce a usable specification
or patch. Load related topics only when the chosen procedure calls for them.

name: apple-hig-column-views
description: Use when choosing, reviewing, or adapting a macOS multi-column hierarchy browser.
---

# Keep the hierarchy path inspectable

Read [the column-view guide](../../references/column-views.md). Treat the following as application advice, not extra component guarantees.

Inspect the hierarchy, traversal frequency, sorting needs, target platform, and create/review/adapt request. Obtain representative deep branches, leaves, and long names. If only a mockup is available, distinguish its visible path from unverified selection/resizing behavior.

Use columns for deep hierarchies frequently traversed forward and backward when table-style attribute sorting is unnecessary. Put the root first. Selecting a parent reveals children in the next column; selecting a leaf can use the following area for a meaningful preview and metadata. Allow widths to expose long names instead of making truncation the only access. If attribute comparison/sorting dominates, choose a table/outline. This component is macOS-specific; for iPadOS/visionOS evaluate a split view rather than claiming native column-browser support.

Implement the hierarchy browser, produce a selection-to-column contract, or review concrete path/preview defects. Define what happens to downstream columns when the selected ancestor changes so stale descendants cannot appear associated with the new branch.

**Worked transformation:** Before: an asset browser starts at the most recent folder, and selecting a different parent leaves the former leaf preview visible. Decision: the path is ambiguous and preview identity is stale. After: restore a visible root-first path and clear/recompute descendant columns and preview on ancestor changes.

Deliver the artifact with root, parent/leaf rules, resize policy, and preview contents. Traverse sibling branches, return to root, resize a long-name column, and select a leaf. Fail for detached descendants, a preview of the wrong item, or no route to root. State native keyboard/accessibility traversal as unverified if not exercised.

Load [outline-views](../apple-hig-outline-views/SKILL.md) for sorted hierarchy attributes or [split-views](../apple-hig-split-views/SKILL.md) for supported cross-platform adaptation.

# Column views Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/column-views) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. A macOS column browser displays one hierarchy level per vertical column. A parent row has a triangle; selecting it reveals its children in the next column, supporting movement into a branch and back to earlier levels. For hierarchical presentation on iPadOS or visionOS, evaluate a split view instead. ## Best practices Use columns for deep hierarchies that people frequently traverse in both directions when table-style sorting is unnecessary. Put the root at the first column so returning to the beginning is predictable. At a leaf, consider using the next area for a preview and useful metadata, such as creation or modification date, type, or size. Allow column resizing so long names remain available. ## Platform considerations This component is for macOS; it is unsupported in iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, visionOS, and watchOS. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Lists and tables](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/lists-and-tables) [Outline views](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/outline-views) [Split views](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/split-views) #### Developer documentation — AppKit

# Apple HIG: Platform and task adaptation

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify the person’s primary task and the target platform before translating a screen. Read that platform’s procedure; use Principles to resolve hierarchy and Designing for games only for gameplay.
2. Compare navigation, window/scene model, primary input, attention duration and state restoration. Preserve the product task while changing the interaction appropriate to the destination platform.
3. For device changes such as opening an iPhone Duo or resizing an iPad window, specify what selection, editing state and route survive each transition.

name: apple-hig-designing-for-macos
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting a Mac experience for multiple windows, menu commands, keyboard workflows, precise selection, or desktop file work.
---

# Give desktop work desktop control

Read [Designing for macOS](../../references/designing-for-macos.md). Inspect the current task, document/content model, windows, commands, and interruption behavior. Determine whether the request is a design, review, or port. Preserve the existing stack and distinguish observed behavior from proposals or missing runtime evidence.

Choose window boundaries around useful units of work. If documents or parallel comparisons benefit from independent windows, retain their own selections and edits. If one workspace suffices, make it resizable and avoid unnecessary modal navigation. Plan full screen for focused work without making it the only usable arrangement. Keep essential commands reachable even when a window is partly offscreen.

Build a command inventory from the task. Put app commands in the menu bar, give common operations appropriate shortcuts, and ensure a keyboard-only completion path. Align toolbar/contextual controls with those same actions and availability states. Use pointer precision for selection and editing rather than inflating a phone-style interface across the display. Preserve conventional file opening/saving and relevant Dock-menu behavior.

Specify app activation changes: switching away and back must preserve work and clearly distinguish the active target for commands. Offer customization where different work styles justify it, such as tools or window arrangement; do not require customization before basic use.

**Before → decision → after:** A photo catalog port displays every album as a full-screen drill-down and exposes Export only through a floating touch menu. Desktop comparison needs persistent context and a discoverable command. After, an album sidebar and resizable detail area support selection; File > Export and a keyboard command act on that selection, and optional second windows compare collections without losing the original state.

Deliver the revised window/command model or implementation, with a keyboard path and activation scenario. Fail if menu and toolbar act on different selections, switching apps loses edits, or resizing hides the only completion action. Linux inspection does not establish actual menu-bar integration, multi-display behavior, or native keyboard accessibility.

Use [Keyboards](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-keyboards/SKILL.md) for command details, [Layout](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-layout/SKILL.md) for window constraints, and [Mac Catalyst](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-mac-catalyst/SKILL.md) when adapting an iPad app through that technology.

# Designing for macOS Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-macos) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Mac use ranges from quick tasks to hours of focused work, often with many applications and displays. People typically sit 1–3 feet away at a desk; external displays and an iPad may extend the workspace. ## Best practices - Use the large display to reduce nested navigation and modal workflows while keeping density comfortable to read. - Let people resize, reposition, show, and hide windows, including across displays; support full screen for concentration. - Put the app’s commands in the menu bar and provide useful keyboard shortcuts, including complete keyboard workflows. - Support precise selections and edits with mouse and trackpad, plus keyboards, game controllers, and Siri where appropriate. - Handle transitions between active and inactive apps smoothly without losing context. - Offer relevant customization of toolbars, window configurations, colors, and fonts. - Integrate familiar menu bar, file management, full-screen, and Dock-menu behavior rather than importing another platform’s interaction assumptions. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-macos) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here.

name: apple-hig-writing
description: Use when drafting or reviewing interface labels, instructions, empty states, errors, settings, or other product language for Apple-platform tasks.
---

# Write the action and the remedy people need

Read [Writing](../../references/writing.md). Inspect the actual flow, terminology, audience, component, device/input, and requested design/review/adaptation scope. Preserve product meaning and existing voice while changing copy. If a screenshot omits the triggering behavior, qualify the interpretation rather than inventing an error cause.

Identify the person's current question: what happened, what can I do, or what should I enter? Put that information first. Use clear action verbs and link destinations; keep terminology/capitalization consistent across entry, continuation, and completion. Adjust seriousness to context without changing the product's identity. Name the correct input action for the target device rather than telling a TV viewer to tap.

Choose the surface along with the words. An ordinary correction belongs near its field; urgent required attention may justify an alert. Label every field and provide usable formats/examples. If an error repeats, inspect whether the interaction can prevent it before polishing the message. Empty states should offer a useful next action, but essential permanent instructions should not exist only before content arrives. Settings should describe their enabled behavior and link directly where possible.

Remove needless words, ambiguous responsibility, perspective shifts, and culture-bound cleverness. Read revised copy aloud and check it in the actual component; concise wording that conceals consequences is not an improvement. Consider screen-reader access and shared/distant displays.

**Before → decision → after:** A booking form says “Oops! Invalid” after rejecting a time, with “Click here” below. Decision: the person needs the permitted time and an action. After, a nearby message reads “Choose a time between 9:00 AM and 5:00 PM,” and the control says “Choose another time.” The same term “appointment” persists through confirmation.

Deliver replacement strings in context or the updated artifact, explaining meaningful behavioral assumptions. Fail if a label hides its outcome, correction still gives no remedy, or translation/large text removes essential meaning. Source review establishes wording, not actual localized pronunciation or screen-reader behavior unless tested.

Use [Inclusion](../apple-hig-inclusion/SKILL.md) for assumptions and representation, [Privacy](../apple-hig-privacy/SKILL.md) for purpose strings, or [Accessibility](../apple-hig-accessibility/SKILL.md) for semantic access.

# Writing Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/writing) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Treat language as an integral interface element in onboarding, alerts, accessibility descriptions, and ordinary tasks. ## Getting started Choose a consistent voice based on the audience, familiar vocabulary, and desired feeling; maintain a terminology list. Adjust tone to the situation, such as a serious payment failure versus an achievement celebration, without changing identity. Remove unnecessary words and read copy aloud to test clarity. Use plain, nongendered, localizable wording and consider screen-reader access. ## Best practices - Start each screen with its most important information. Format for scanning and divide unrelated ideas or complex sequences across suitable screens. - Label actions with clear verbs and links with their actual destination/purpose, avoiding clever substitutes or generic click-here wording. # Make commands discoverable and preserve familiar keys

Read [Keyboards](../../references/keyboards.md). Inspect task commands, text-entry contexts, current bindings, supported platforms/locales, and requested design/review/adaptation. Physical keyboards are covered on every listed platform except watchOS. Preserve the existing stack and identify actual keyboard evidence before claiming complete navigation.

Build a command inventory from frequent actions. Reuse familiar standard shortcuts for their expected meanings; consult the guide's mapping in context rather than treating legacy/system entries as universally available app APIs. A standard combination may serve another meaning only when its normal action has no place in this app. Avoid deriving an unrelated command by adding modifiers to a familiar one.

For app-specific commands, prefer a learnable Command-based combination, Shift for related variants, and sparing Option; avoid Control conflicts. Check international keyboards where Option makes characters. Preserve expected modifier-drag/resize behavior and clear smallest-increment arrow adjustment. Games may use single keys and customization while retaining system actions.

Trace ordinary content focus and Full Keyboard Access separately. On iPad, content/text/sidebar/collection focus is not proof that every button/switch is reachable; Full Keyboard Access supplies the broader route. Preserve accessibility shortcuts. On visionOS, make each Command-discoverability title meaningful without submenu context because the displayed list is flattened.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a diagram app uses Command-C to create a shape, binds Control-based shortcuts for everything, and has an unreachable Done button. Decision: copy semantics and a complete keyboard task outweigh shortcut novelty. After, Command-C copies selection, shape creation gets a suitable distinct command, and focus/activation can reach Done; the command title explains itself in discoverability UI.

Deliver a corrected command/binding inventory and keyboard task path or implementation. Fail if text editing invokes an unrelated command, shortcuts collide with system access, or the task cannot finish without a pointer. Actual OS shortcuts, international layouts, and Full Keyboard Access need supported-device execution; static binding inspection is narrower evidence.

Use [Focus and selection](../apple-hig-focus-and-selection/SKILL.md) for grouping/order or [Game controls](../apple-hig-game-controls/SKILL.md) for gameplay-specific bindings.

# Revised Mac specimen archive browser

This is a framework-agnostic interaction contract, based on "'`interface.md`. It specifies a resizable macOS workspace for traversing deep specimen folders. It requires no Apple SDK. The brief establishes three unrelated columns (search results, status, size), loss of parent context, long folder names, and frequent empty folders; it supplies no running interface or representative archive. Examples below are synthetic.

## Decisions

Replace the three fixed-purpose columns with a root-first hierarchy browser. Each vertical column represents one hierarchy level, never an attribute. Root column contains the named archive root; selecting it reveals its immediate children. Selecting a folder reveals its children immediately to the right and leaves every selected ancestor visible when space permits. Folder rows have a trailing navigation triangle, including empty folders; files do not. Single selection per level defines one unambiguous branch.

This follows [Column views — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/column-views#Best-practices): columns suit deep, frequently traversed hierarchies when table-style sorting is unnecessary. The brief supplies no requirement to sort or compare status/size. Default to name ordering; status and size remain available for the selected item. If attribute comparison becomes the primary task, reconsider a table or outline rather than turning hierarchy columns back into attributes.

Use the next area after a selected file for a detail summary: full name, full archive-relative location, type, status, and size with units. Show “Unknown” for unavailable metadata; never substitute zero. A file preview is optional and appears only if its format is supported; the summary always works without it. Folder status and size can appear in a summary below the browser, identified by the selected folder'"'s full name. Folder size is “Not calculated” unless supplied; browsing must not require recursive size calculation. Metadata placement and these strings are product decisions; HIG suggests considering useful leaf previews and metadata, rather than requiring a particular preview implementation.

Do not retain search results as a hierarchy level. Any existing search surface remains separate. Its result-to-browser handoff must resolve the selected result's ancestor IDs from the archive root, then select and reveal that branch. If resolution fails, keep the current branch and report the unavailable result; never invent a parent relationship. Search query, ranking, and search UI redesign are outside this brief.

## Selection and state contract

Store stable item IDs, parent IDs, node kind, per-column width and vertical scroll position. Names are labels, not identity. The archive root is the navigation boundary.

"'```text
state = { rootId, selectedChain, columns, focusedColumn, requestGeneration }

selectRow(level, itemId):
    require itemId belongs to columns[level]
    increment requestGeneration
    selectedChain = selectedChain before level + itemId
    discard columns after level and all previous preview/metadata
    mark item selected; make level the focused column
    if item is file:
        show summary bound to itemId
    else:
        append child column bound to itemId, initially loading
        request children(itemId, requestGeneration)

receiveChildren(parentId, generation, result):
    ignore unless generation is current and parentId is selectedChain.last
    replace loading area with rows, empty state, or error
    do not automatically select a child
```

The root is selected on first entry, revealing its contents. Selecting a sibling ancestor immediately clears the former descendants, even while new data loads. Every metadata response uses the same selected-ID/generation guard. A late response cannot reintroduce another branch or preview.

An empty folder remains a folder: keep its row selected and show “This folder is empty” in its child column. Provide “Go to Parent”; at the archive root this action is unavailable. A pending request says “Loading folder…”; an unsuccessful request says “Couldn’t load this folder” with “Retry.” Never interpret failure or pending work as emptiness. These are proposed states for potentially asynchronous archives, not observed implementation defects. Clear, actionable empty/error copy follows [Writing — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/writing#Best-practices).

Go to Parent truncates the chain by one item, retains the parent selection and its children column, and focuses that parent'"'s row. At a file, this selects its containing folder. Go to Archive Root selects root, removes deeper selections, reveals root children, and scrolls the browser to its beginning. Neither command leaves old detail content visible. Switching to another app and back preserves the branch, widths, scroll positions, and command target.

## Width, depth, and input

Allow independently resizable columns. Starting values are product defaults, not HIG measurements: 240 logical points wide, minimum 160. Do not impose a name-length-based maximum. A divider drag changes only that column and preserves selection. Offer View > Fit Selected Column to Name as a keyboard alternative; it measures the longest loaded label in that column plus row adornments. Overflow uses horizontal scrolling rather than shrinking every column into illegibility.

Names use one row with middle truncation when necessary. The selected-item summary always exposes the complete, selectable, wrapping name and location, including for folders. Resizing therefore is not the only way to read a name. Do not rely on hover alone. Names with identical visible fragments remain distinguishable by selecting them and reading their full names.

On descent, scroll horizontally only enough to reveal the new child column and its selected parent where feasible. At narrow widths, earlier columns can move offscreen; retain them in the scrollable strip. Go to Parent and Go to Archive Root remain available through the menu regardless of horizontal position. Resizing a window never changes the branch or converts columns into attributes. These overflow policies are product choices applying HIG's root-first and resizable-column guidance.

Use one resizable workspace; support ordinary window and full-screen arrangements without requiring full screen. Put navigation commands in a Go menu and sizing in View. Menu and any visible control invoke the same state transitions and enabled states. This applies [Designing for macOS — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-macos#Best-practices).

Proposed keyboard contract while the browser owns focus:

| Action | Input and outcome |
|---|---|
| Select sibling | Up/Down selects adjacent row and applies the same selection transition as a click; stops at list boundaries. |
| Enter folder | Right moves to its child column and selects its first row, if loaded and nonempty; otherwise stays on the parent. |
| Return | Left invokes Go to Parent; no change at root. |
| Reach all commands | Menu navigation exposes Go to Parent, Go to Archive Root, Retry when applicable, and Fit Selected Column to Name. |
| Move between controls | Tab/Shift-Tab follows the host's keyboard navigation policy; no keyboard trap. |

Do not intercept browser arrows when a text field or selectable summary text owns focus. Distinguish focused target from persistent ancestor selection visually. No custom global shortcut is required. Preserve system and text-editing shortcuts; actual menu reachability and Full Keyboard Access require later Mac testing. These requirements apply [Keyboards — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/keyboards#Best-practices); the exact browser arrow mapping is a product decision.

## Worked before/after

Synthetic branch:

"'```text
Specimen Archive / Marine Invertebrates /
North Atlantic Expedition 1902 — Station 014 — Preserved Reference Specimens /
Tray A / specimen-0042.tif
```

Before, as described by the brief: the three columns mean Search Results, Status, and File Size. Choosing Tray A loses its parent context; the brief does not establish how that loss is rendered or what resizing does.

After selecting through Tray A:

```text
[Specimen Archive ▸] | [Marine Invertebrates ▸] | [North Atlantic…Specimens ▸] | [Tray A ▸] | specimen-0042.tif
```

Each bracketed row is a persistent ancestor selection in its own level. Widen the expedition column or read its full name in the selected-folder summary. Select the file: its parent chain remains and the following area shows its summary, including its full location. Change the expedition selection to sibling “Pacific Expedition 1903”: Tray A, the file column, and the file summary disappear immediately; only the Pacific children can populate the next column. If Pacific contains an empty “Uncatalogued” folder, selecting it retains the Pacific path and shows the empty-folder message with Go to Parent. Returning to root reveals the archive'"'s children without any stale specimen preview.

## Acceptance checks and evidence limits

Static specification checks passed: the contract assigns one hierarchy level per column; retains ancestor IDs; defines descendant invalidation, root return, leaf summary, long-name access, empty-folder behavior, width/overflow policy, and keyboard actions. These are document checks, not execution results.

The supplied design fails the stated task at the brief level: its three columns represent unrelated information and choosing a child loses parent context. No additional runtime defects were observed.

All implementation checks below are **not executed**. Each is a required acceptance scenario for a future implementation:

| Check | Pass condition |
|---|---|
| Deep traversal | Traverse six levels; each selected child has the selected parent immediately to its left in the model. Horizontal scrolling recovers every ancestor. |
| Sibling change and races | Switch an ancestor while old child/metadata requests are pending. Former descendants clear immediately; delayed responses never appear in the new branch. |
| Root return | From a leaf and from a horizontally scrolled narrow window, Go to Archive Root reveals root children and clears stale detail. |
| Long names | Use two 200-character names with matching prefixes. Resize and fit the column; select each and read/copy its complete name from the summary without hover. |
| Empty folder | Empty folder stays selected; child area reports emptiness and Go to Parent returns correctly. Loading and error are distinguishable from empty. |
| Leaf identity | Select two different files; each summary's name, location and metadata match only the current file. Unknown size is never displayed as zero. |
| Narrow/expanded window | Resize while deep in a branch. IDs, selection and widths survive; scroll and menu routes remain usable. |
| Keyboard task | Without a pointer, reach a deep file, inspect its name, visit an empty sibling folder, fit a column, retry a failure, and return to root. Text editing retains its normal keys. |
| Activation and command consistency | Switch apps and return; selection survives. Menu and visible actions target the same selected ID. |
| Mac access verification | Exercise Full Keyboard Access and assistive-technology traversal on a Mac; verify focus visibility, full names, hierarchy relationships, and empty/error announcements. |

Only local "'`interface.md` and installed skill instructions/references were used; no web browsing occurred. Official links identify the sources recorded in the local snapshots, dated 2026-10-25; they were not fetched or independently verified. Root skill, relevant family routes, topic procedures, and their guides were explicitly read from the installed package; the topic index was searched for matching concepts. No device, SDK, GUI, build, performance, keyboard, localization, or accessibility execution occurred. No archive samples establish real depth, latency, name distributions, metadata semantics, or sorting needs. Defaults and synthetic examples therefore require validation with representative specimen archives.
EOF'
